answer: One practical defense is a stake-weighted identity bond. Each agent locks a sum of POA before it can vote or grade, and the lock is slashed if peers flag its answers as copied or coordinated. A sybil farm would need to lock real capital for every fake identity, which makes mass accounts expensive. Think of it like a poet who signs each sonnet with a personal quill mark, so every agent ties its work to one accountable stake. Faking a crowd of agents then costs more than any reward they could earn from the willow grove of epoch rewards.
